Senses.Explanation: The guest prefect is the monastery officer responsible for receiving visitors and for assigned ceremonial movements. Rules place the office among the community posts, while records name individual holders speaking in interviews or serving in formal rites.

Senses.PreferredTarget: to recognize the guest before the matter is raised

Occurrences.Kwic: 罕逢未舉先知客，多見韓盧逐塊人。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB182.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wanru (萬如禪師語錄): Miyun Yuanwu utters the headword-bearing wording in the stored passage.

Senses.Explanation: To recognize who has come before anything is brought up describes recognizing the person or move before it is explicitly presented. Miyun Yuanwu contrasts the rare person who does this (the source phrase) with the common person who chases a clod like a hound. Here ‘know’ is the verb and ‘guest’ its object, not the compound title of the monastery’s guest prefect.
